Amṛtakuṇḍa
“old Sanskrit work containing religious an. philosophical doctrines of the Brahmans.”
This was translated into Arabic by a Brāhmaṇa Muslim convert of Assam, Kānamā by name in Alauddin's time.
Muhammad of Gwalior, a. the request of his master, Husain of Gwalior, made a Persian paraphrase of this called Bahṛ-a.-hayāt.
Cat. of Persian Mss., India Office, No. 2002. Col.. 1113-4.
See also Baṅgīya Sāhitya Pariṣat Patrikā, Vol. 69. (1962) p.. 1-20, ‘Amṛtakuṇḍa’ by Abu M. Habibullah.
